transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess… I got kind of carried away with this park idea. I’m usually just one of the crew guys, but I was trying to run like three bids, calling city people, lining up plant suppliers, messaging everybody I knew about it. It was like I couldn’t really shut it off.
During that time, did you feel unusually high or euphoric?

Yeah… kind of. I don’t know if I’d call it happy exactly, but I felt really fired up, like bigger than myself. And if somebody at work questioned the plan or told me to slow down, I’d snap at them way harder than I should’ve.
During that time, were you sleeping much less than usual and still feeling like you had plenty of energy?
I’m not really sure. I mean… my sleep was off, but I wasn’t exactly keeping track. I just know I was up late some nights with all that stuff on my mind.
During that time, did you hear or see things that other people couldn’t?
No… I don’t think so. I mean, I was keyed up, but I wasn’t seeing stuff or hearing voices or anything like that.
Have you ever had a period where you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day for at least two weeks?
Yeah. It’s been… more than two weeks. Honestly it’s felt like this has been hanging over me for about a year, and lately it’s been the worst it’s gotten.
During that fired-up period, did you need much less sleep than usual?
I don’t really know. Maybe a little less some nights, but I can’t say I needed less sleep exactly. I just wasn’t paying close attention.
During that fired-up period, did it cause serious problems in your life, like getting you into major trouble at work or with other people?

Not major trouble, no… but it’s been affecting work. I’ve been missing details on bids and measurements, and in my line of work that can turn into a real problem. I worry one bad mistake could cost me clients, or worse, get someone hurt on a job site.
Were you using any drugs or alcohol around the time you got that unusually fired up?
I don’t really know. I mean… nothing that stands out to me. I wasn’t tracking it like that.
During that fired-up period, were you talking more than usual?
I’m not really sure. Maybe I was a little more chatty at times, but I didn’t notice it as some big change.
During that fired-up period, did you feel unusually important, powerful, or capable of doing things that were beyond what you’d normally think you could do?

Yeah… I guess so. I had this idea I was about to be the guy every town around here would call for sustainable landscaping. Which sounds kind of… big, saying it now. I’m still just trying to keep my smaller jobs paid up.
During that fired-up period, were you taking on a lot more projects or activities than you usually would?

Yeah. I mean… more than usual, definitely. I went from just being a crew guy to trying to juggle a bunch of bids, calling city people, lining up plant suppliers, messaging people about that park idea. It was like I couldn’t really shut it off.
About how many days in a row did that fired-up period last?
About two weeks, I think. It started when I got into that whole park pitch thing… trying to remake myself a bit. Then I kind of crashed after that.
During that fired-up time, did your thoughts feel like they were racing?

Yeah… they did. My head was just going fast, like plant lists and slogans and layouts for the park, who I had to talk to, who I had to impress. I’d write pages in a notebook and still feel like I was behind.
During that fired-up period, were you much more active or driven to get things done than you usually are?
Yeah. I was… pretty driven, I guess. I’d be up before daylight loading tools, sketching out beds, pricing native plants. Then after working outside all day, I still felt like I had to keep going.
During that fired-up period, were you hospitalized because of it?
No… I wasn’t hospitalized for it.
Have you ever had another time in your life when you felt unusually high, irritable, or full of energy like that?

Yeah… there was another time like that. Before I sort of crashed, I felt really fired up, like… bigger than myself, I guess. And I was touchy. If a coworker questioned my plan or told me to slow down, I’d snap at him way harder than I should’ve.
Besides the park-pitch time, was there another separate period in your life when you felt unusually high, irritable, or full of energy?

Yeah… separate from that, there was a stretch before I crashed where I felt really fired up. Kind of… bigger than myself. But I was also quick to snap if someone at work questioned what I was doing or told me to slow down.
Thinking of that other separate fired-up time, did it happen at a different point in your life from the park-pitch episode?
I’m… not totally sure. It feels like it was separate, but I don’t really have the timing clear in my head.
Were those fired-up times separated by a period when your mood and energy had gone back to your usual self?
I don’t know. I’m having a hard time separating it out like that. There were times I felt more normal, I guess, but I can’t really say for sure how it lined up.
Before this park-pitch episode, was there ever another separate time in your life when you felt unusually high, irritable, or full of energy?

Yeah… before I crashed, there was a time I felt really fired up. Like, bigger than myself, I guess. But I’d also snap at guys at work if they questioned my plan or told me to slow down… more than I should’ve.
